correctness.rationale: For normalized conjugate-linear duality map J_p(x)=norm(x)^(2-p)(|x_i|^(p-2)conj(x_i)), evaluate at e_j+t e_k to obtain exact identity J_p(v+tw)=(1+t^p)^((2-p)/p)[J_p(v)+t^(p-1)J_p(w)]. For p<2, t^(p-1) dominates O(t) response at each nonzero v coordinate, forcing disjoint column supports. For p>2, first real derivative in w vanishes while real Hessian of norm² is bounded below by norm(v)^(2-p) sum_i |v_i|^(p-2)|w_i|², again implying disjoint supports. Basis evaluations identify row j with J_p(column j); disjoint columns and row-column support equality yield exactly one nonzero per row and column or T=0 (mixed zero/nonzero columns contradicted by scaling factor). Resulting support permutation is involutive, weights obey a_pi(j)=conj(a_j), and two-column coefficient comparison forces equal modulus c>0. Weighted involutive isometry satisfies converse by the duality map isometry covariance. Then T²=c²Id excludes compact T on infinite ell_p; p=2 exception explicit. Argument accommodates complex phases, countable supports within arbitrary I. Random matrix spot checks in package are only diagnostics; classification proof is analytic.
